geo_headlines: TRUMP: 'NO, I HAVEN'T' DECIDED ON MASSIVE ATTACK — Fri Oval Office, walked back timing on 'massive attack' rhetoric. Said Iran is now 'serious' in talks. Retained option; described choice between deal or 'much higher level' of strikes. Red line remains proximity to nuclear weapon capability.

13TH CONSECUTIVE NIGHT US STRIKES ON IRAN completed — CENTCOM continued operations targeting Iran maritime-threat capability. Reported strikes on Revolutionary Guards Navy base in Ziba Kenar (Caspian coast) and Piranshahr near Iraq border. Missile strike on Ahvaz reportedly killed 4, injured 5 per Iranian state media.

IRAN CLAIMS RETALIATION ON US BASES IN KUWAIT, BAHRAIN, JORDAN — Revolutionary Guards claim strikes on Camp Buehring (Kuwait), Camp Arifjan, Camp Doha, US surveillance tower in Bahrain. Jordan military reports intercepting missiles/drones with no casualties. Four US service members killed in prior strikes.

SAUDI ARABIA STRIKES YEMEN HODEIDA — Saudi launched strikes on Houthi positions in Hodeida following Houthi Red Sea tanker attacks. New front opened in maritime chokepoint dispute. Bab el-Mandeb now second focal point alongside Hormuz.

CHINA/PAKISTAN PUSH FOR US-IRAN PEACE TALKS — Reports Fri emerged China increasingly engaged in pressing diplomatic path, with Pakistan attempting to revive negotiations. This drove Brent -3.88% to $96.78 and WTI -3.12% to $89.31 from Thu $100+ close. Oil still on pace for weekly +9.7% Brent / +8.3% WTI.
US GAS PRICES $4.10/GAL — AAA national average up 17c from month ago; direct pass-through from oil surge. Fed watching for wage/CPI second-round effects into 7/29 meeting.

SP 500 WEEKLY -0.6%, NASDAQ WEEKLY -3% — first back-to-back weekly declines since March. Big Tech capex angst (GOOGL/TSLA) + oil shock + hawkish rates. Dow rescued by AAPL +3.5% Fri ahead of Wed earnings.

MASSIVE EARNINGS WEEK AHEAD — MSFT + META Tue after close, AAPL + AMZN Wed after close, all in FOMC week. Combined market cap ~$14T. Post-GOOGL capex anxiety, guidance/capex disclosures will be scrutinized.
headline: Weekend hold pattern: Trump 'no' on immediate attack, China pushing US-Iran talks, oil retreated -4% Fri from $100 spike. S&P +0.05% Fri (weekly -0.6%), Nasdaq weekly -3%. Big week ahead: MSFT+META Tue AC, AAPL+AMZN Wed AC, FOMC Wed 2pm.
client_frame: This is a weekend edition, so no overnight tape churn, but the setup for Monday matters. Friday closed a genuinely volatile week — the S&P finished essentially flat at 7,411.98 (+0.05%) after Thursday's -1.2% oil-shock plunge, the Dow recovered 0.46% on a 3.5% pop in Apple (repositioning ahead of its Wednesday after-close earnings), and the Nasdaq Composite lost another 0.64% to close down 3% on the week — its worst since March. Two consecutive weekly declines for S&P and Nasdaq is the first such streak of the year. Under the surface, three storylines are now interlocking. First, the Big Tech capex reality-check that started with GOOGL and TSLA last week is being repriced across the whole complex. Chip stocks got smoked again Friday (SanDisk -11%) on continued AI-spending concerns, even as Intel's Thursday-night blowout — Q2 revenue $16.13B versus $14.43B consensus, the biggest beat in 15 years, Data Center +59% — provided a partial counterexample. Second, the Iran/oil channel is now in a fragile equilibrium. Brent closed Thursday $100.69 for the first time since May, then dropped 3.88% Friday to $96.78 on reports that China and Pakistan are pushing to revive US-Iran peace negotiations. WTI mirrored the move, settling $89.31 after touching $92.50 pre-market. But the underlying supply risk has not gone away — Brent is up ~9.7% on the week, WTI +8.3%, Houthi Red Sea attacks continue, Saudi retaliated by striking Yemen's Hodeida overnight. Trump Friday said 'no, I haven't' when asked if he'd decided on a massive attack, and characterized Iran as now 'serious' in talks — a de-escalation in rhetoric, not in kinetic activity (13th consecutive night of US strikes completed). AAA national gasoline hit $4.10 a gallon, up 17 cents on the month. Third, the FOMC is Wednesday. Cumulative +25bp is 82% priced into September, and this week's macro releases will move that. The 10Y closed Friday 4.679% (-2.4bp on the day), still near a new conflict-period high — the rate market is not softening. What matters for Monday and the week ahead: this is the single biggest earnings week of the season. MSFT and META report Tuesday after close, AAPL and AMZN Wednesday after close, all sandwiched around the FOMC decision Wednesday 2pm ET plus GDP Thursday and PCE Friday. Combined mega-cap market cap of ~$14 trillion. After GOOGL got tattooed for a $195-205B capex guide and negative FCF, and TSLA for a 1.4% operating margin, MSFT and META guidance discipline will be scrutinized more intensely than in prior quarters. Positioning framing: the risk stool remains three-legged — capex fatigue, Iran/oil, hawkish Fed. If any two of those three ease in the same week, we get a squeeze higher. If any one intensifies, the S&P 7,400 support becomes the tell. Weekend headline risk is asymmetric to the downside — a Trump 'massive attack' announcement or a Houthi tanker hit would gap oil back through $100 and equity futures well below Friday's close. Hedges from Thursday paid; keep them on through the FOMC and mega-cap earnings. Do not add fresh equity risk before Wednesday. If MSFT/META guide clean AI-capex numbers and Powell threads the needle on inflation asymmetry, that is the earliest window to reduce hedges — not before.
